title: The Holiday Budget That Doesn't Follow You Into March

lines.say: Are you still paying for last Christmas?
Let's make sure this year doesn't follow you into next fall.

scene.text: Holiday spending on a credit card is a loan, not a gift.

lines.say: Because holiday spending on a credit card isn't really a gift. It's a loan, with interest.
So here's a holiday budget that fits the cash you actually have, in five steps, with real numbers.
Step one. Start with the cash, not the list.

scene.label: Cash for the holidays
scene.sub: savings + the goal money from December's paychecks

lines.cap: Say you have $600, between savings and the goal money from your December paychecks.
lines.say: Say you have six hundred dollars, between savings and the goal money from your December paychecks.
That number is the budget. Not your credit limit.
Step two. Write the real list. Every person, and every cost that isn't a gift.
Here's the gift list.
Partner, one fifty.
Two kids, one twenty each.
Both parents, sixty each.
Three siblings, forty each.
Four friends, twenty each.
And the work gift swap, twenty-five.
Then, the costs nobody puts on the list.
Gas to visit family, ninety.
Hosting dinner, one forty.
Wrapping and cards, thirty-five.
Shipping, forty.

scene.label: The real total
scene.sub: $440 more than the cash you have

lines.cap: Add it up, and the real total is $1,040. That's $440 more than the cash.
lines.say: Add it up, and the real total is ten forty. That's four hundred and forty dollars more than the cash.
Step three. Don't borrow the gap.

scene.head: $440 on a 24% card, paying $50 a month

rows.label: Put the gap on the card

scene.foot: Still paying for Christmas in October.

lines.cap: Put the gap on a credit card at 24%, pay $50 a month, and it takes 10 months and about $49 in interest.
lines.say: Put the gap on a credit card at twenty-four percent, pay fifty a month, and it takes ten months, and about fifty dollars in interest.
You'd still be paying for this Christmas in October.

scene.text: Not paid off by the January statement? It's a loan.

lines.say: So here's the rule. If you can't pay it off by the January statement, it's not a gift. It's a loan.
Step four. Trim by priority, not by guilt.
Start with the gifts.

lines.cap: Partner goes from $150 to $100. The kids, $200 total.
lines.say: Partner goes from one fifty to a hundred. The kids, two hundred total.
Parents, thirty each.

lines.cap: Three siblings? Suggest a Secret Santa, and you buy one $40 gift instead of three.
lines.say: Three siblings? Suggest a Secret Santa, and you buy one forty-dollar gift instead of three.

lines.cap: Friends get homemade cookies, about $20 of ingredients.
lines.say: Friends get homemade cookies, about twenty dollars of ingredients.

lines.cap: And skip the work swap this year. Gifts go from $735 to $420.
lines.say: And skip the work swap this year. Gifts go from seven thirty-five, to four twenty.
Then the hidden costs.
Gas stays. You still want to see your family.

lines.cap: Make dinner a potluck, and hosting drops to $60.
lines.say: Make dinner a potluck, and hosting drops to sixty.

lines.cap: Plain paper and twine instead of fancy wrap: $10. Order early and ship less: $20.
lines.say: Plain paper and twine instead of fancy wrap, ten dollars. Order early and ship less, twenty.
Hidden costs go from three oh five, to one eighty.

scene.label: New total: $420 + $180
scene.sub: = the cash you have. Nothing borrowed.

lines.cap: $420 plus $180 is $600. Exactly the cash you have, and nothing follows you into next year.
lines.say: Four twenty, plus one eighty, is six hundred dollars. Exactly the cash you have, and nothing follows you into next year.
Step five. Fix next year, in January.

lines.cap: Start a holiday sinking fund with your first January paycheck. $600 over 24 paychecks is $25 each.
lines.say: Start a holiday sinking fund with your first paycheck in January. Six hundred dollars over twenty-four paychecks is twenty-five dollars each.

scene.text: Next December, the cash is already there.

lines.say: Next December, you start with the cash already there. Episode three walks through exactly how.
